our_argument_summary: V13 reduced cross-equatorial error 25-78% to 6.2% RMSE by adding a fitted equatorial ring radius (14,105 km) tuned to the same six WGS84 city-pair routes used for validation — in-sample retrodiction, not prediction. NH accuracy regressed 5.2%→7.3%. Four-plus fitted parameters vs WGS84's two; 6.2% vs sub-0.01% relative accuracy (620x). OPEN-015 carves out an explicit lat<~12 deg exclusion zone. The verdict text additionally dismantles the AIC/BIC defense: AICc collapses at n=6/k=4 (40 penalty units, denominator exactly 1, divergence at n=5), asymptotic IC justification unreached at n=6, and ICs adjudicate among candidates but cannot rescue a model absolutely worse than a non-nested competitor.

holes_found.description: tldr_verdict pairs the 600x multiplier with the wrong baseline: 'still 600x worse than standard geodesy's sub-centimeter accuracy.' The 600x figure derives from the relative-error comparison (6.2% / 0.01% = 620), which is how finding and detail_evidence correctly state it ('sub-0.01%'). Taken literally against a sub-centimeter absolute baseline, 6.2% RMSE on a ~10,000 km route (~620 km error vs ~1 cm) is a factor of ~6x10^7, not 600x. A defender who multiplies it out can claim our headline TLDR understates by five orders of magnitude — or, worse, that we don't understand our own numbers. The ordering claim (dome much worse) holds, so this is imprecision, not a factual reversal; per TLDR severity guidance this stays minor.
holes_found.recommendation: In tldr_verdict, replace 'standard geodesy's sub-centimeter accuracy' with 'standard geodesy's sub-0.01% accuracy' (mirrors the finding field). One-phrase edit; makes the TLDR's ratio and baseline arithmetically consistent.

holes_found.description: Baseline proliferation across the WIN-027/057/069 detail_group: WIN-027's finding cites 'sub-millimetre precision' (Vincenty algorithmic accuracy), WIN-057 cites 'sub-0.01%' / 600x (relative error), WIN-069 cites '~5 orders of magnitude worse than sub-meter geodesy' (absolute positional accuracy). All three are individually correct in their own units, but they appear side-by-side in the same rendered group, comparing the SAME 6.2% RMSE to three different baselines and yielding multipliers from 600x to 10^5. A critic can juxtapose them as 'the reviewers can't decide how much worse the dome is.'
holes_found.recommendation: Harmonize with a labeling clause rather than changing numbers: e.g., WIN-057 finding '600x worse in relative-error terms (sub-0.01%)' and WIN-069 '~5 orders of magnitude worse in absolute position terms (sub-meter geodesy)'. Three small clause insertions; preempts the compilation attack without altering any verified figure.

kernel_of_truth.description: The V13 improvement is real arithmetic: cross-equatorial residuals on the six showcase routes did fall from 25-78% to 6.2% RMSE (wins.json:WIN-057.detail_evidence), and the dome author's iterative-refinement instinct — flagged as a genuine engineering virtue in our own text via the Clarke 1866 comparison (wins.json:WIN-057.detail_verdict_text) — reflects honest model iteration documented in the dome's own changelog (raw-text/04-coordinates.txt 'Cross-equator: 25-78% on long pairs, under revision').
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Residual reduction by adding a parameter fitted to the validation set is guaranteed, not informative (wins.json:WIN-057.detail_evidence 'adding a free parameter to fit six known routes will always reduce residuals'). The improvement coexists with an NH regression (5.2%→7.3%), an explicit equatorial exclusion zone (OPEN-015, wins.json:WIN-057.detail_extra), and a 620x relative-accuracy gap to a two-parameter competitor (Vincenty 1975, doi:10.1179/sre.1975.23.176.88 — verified resolving this run). Iteration toward a worse asymptote is not evidence of underlying truth.

advocate_mode.best_defense: Stepping into the defender's shoes post-patch: 'Your parameter-count comparison is rigged. WGS84 distance computation may use two ellipsoid parameters, but operational geodesy leans on geoid models (EGM2008) with tens of thousands of coefficients — by your own counting standard, the globe model is the most over-parameterized model in science. V13's four parameters are austere by comparison, and our n=6 validation set is simply where the project currently is; Clarke didn't have GPS either. Give the model the routes and the iterations and the RMSE will fall.' Out of character: the geoid-coefficient move fails because horizontal city-pair distances are computed on the ellipsoid alone — the two parameters our text cites are the complete input set for the quantity being compared; geoid coefficients serve heights and gravity, not the inverse-distance problem. The 'give us more routes' move concedes the central point — there is currently no out-of-sample validation — and the iteration argument is already preempted in detail_verdict_text (Clarke 1866 reached <0.5% on continental baselines without exclusion zones). The defense is rhetorically attractive but fails on contact with what is actually computed.

deeper_analysis: Both c5 minor holes are confirmed integrated and integrated correctly: (1) the asymptotic-regime sentence no longer entangles OPEN-015 with AIC's sample-size justification — the new parenthetical explicitly marks the domain restriction as 'a separate and stronger concern... independently of whether the asymptotic approximation holds at n = 6', which is exactly recommendation (b) from c5; (2) the AICc divergence clause landed verbatim-plus (it also adds the denominator-equals-1 observation). No carry-overs remain; unresolved_prior_cycle is empty. The AIC/BIC rebuttal is now the strongest paragraph in the WIN-027/057/069 group — it grants the defender's strongest apparatus and collapses it on its own terms at three independent levels (small-sample arithmetic, asymptotic regime, candidate-set semantics). One stylistic note, not a hole: the AICc parenthetical now states the divergence fact in three escalating restatements and the verdict text has grown to 3,415 chars; if a future readability pass touches this WIN, the parenthetical is the place to compress. The two fresh minors are low-stakes: one TLDR baseline pairing, one cross-WIN baseline-labeling harmonization. Verdict 'Misleading' remains correct — the dome's claim is true arithmetic wrapped in a false epistemic frame (in-sample fit presented as predictive success), which is precisely what the Misleading category is for.
